purpose: Teach: ウロウロ/かっこよく/光り/営む/釣る/働ける/チョン/リョウ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、町を、絶対、ウロウロ、絶対、よく、絶対、歩いたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — when you were young, do you remember how your father used to walk around town all the time? I'm serious.
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward through time. Gentle opening. Slow, deliberate pace—each phrase lands like a stone dropped in still water. Warm nostalgia, not sad. Eyes half-closed, seeing the past more clearly than the present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、軍服姿、絶対、かっこよく、絶対、見えたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. You know, when you were young, your grandfather looked so handsome in his military uniform. Don't you remember, dear? I really do.
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly, tender and present. Tone holds the fondness of someone who still sees that uniform clearly. Measured rhythm, each memory a small gift offered. Slight warmth on 'dear'—intimate without sentimentality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、月の、絶対、光り、絶対、輝く、絶対、夜、絶対、ばあさんと、絶対、散歩したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember those nights walking with you under the moonlight—how it shone so beautifully. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Voice quieter now, almost reverent. The moonlight itself becomes the subject. Breath slows. A pause before 'shone'—he's seeing it again. Trailing gently, not quite a question, more a shared memory offered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お店を、絶対、営む、絶対、夢、絶対、持っていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: You're right. When you were young, your grandfather had such dreams—he wanted to run his own shop, remember? I haven't forgotten, dear.
lines.style: Affirms gently, then shifts to pride. The mention of the shop brings warmth and a hint of gentle sorrow—dreams held and set aside. Voice steady but tender. No hurry in the delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、川で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、お魚、絶対、釣る、絶対、のが、絶対、得意だったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And when you were young, your father was so good at fishing down by the river—do you remember that, Gran?
lines.style: Shifts slightly, a touch of pride in his own father. Voice lighter, more alive. The fishing is vivid to him. Asking Gran more directly now, inviting her in. Warm, almost playful undertone beneath the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、元気いっぱい、絶対、働ける、絶対、体だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do. Your grandfather was so strong then, so full of energy—the kind of body that could work all day. You remember how he was, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Voice settles into admiration. 'Strong' and 'energy' are spoken with quiet pride. Rhythm is steady, honoring. A note of gentle longing—she's acknowledging the time that has passed. Closes with warmth on 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、時代劇の、絶対、チョン、絶対、髷、絶対、お父さん、絶対、よく、絶対、テレビで、絶対、見たぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I used to see your father all the time on those period dramas on television—in those topknot wigs. Do you remember?
lines.style: A spark of lightness here—almost amused at the memory. The 'topknot wigs' carries a faint smile. Voice warmer, less heavy than before. Still wistful but touched with gentle humor. Reaching across to see if she remembers too.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、リョウ、絶対、さんって、絶対、いう、絶対、お友達、絶対、お祖父ちゃんに、絶対、いたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes, I remember! Your grandfather had a friend named Ryou back then—such a good friend to have around. You haven't forgotten that, have you, dear?
lines.style: Brightness returns, almost suddenly. The name 'Ryou' is spoken with affection—she's conjuring him up too. Voice opens wider, more animated. This is shared, vivid territory. Warm and close on 'dear'—they're in it together.
